title: tenant-aware cost heuristics + SafePaths fallback for batching, cache and quant profiles
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Introduce tenant-aware default heuristics for batching, prefix caching TTLs, and quantization tiers.
Add SafePaths fallback policy to avoid regression during aggressive cost-driven tuning.
Expose a lightweight CLI (econ-prober) to preview tenant default recommendations locally.
description:
Context: we continue to see recurring operator effort tuning per-tenant defaults for batching, cache TTL and quantization when tenants migrate from POC to production. Motivation: reduce manual friction and provide safe automated defaults that improve unit economics without regressing latency or correctness. This PR introduces a tenant-aware cost heuristics layer plus a runtime "SafePaths" fallback that ensures conservative behavior during rollout.

Summary of changes: 1) tenant heuristics engine: new config layer that combines tenant traffic shape metrics (qps, median/p95 seq len, realtime/async tag) with tenant tier (free/paid/enterprise) and historical unit-econ signals to produce a suggested defaults blob: {batch_size_target, batch_wait_ms, prefix_cache_ttl_ms, quant_tier}. 2) cost profile "quant ladder": three preservative quant tiers (Q8-safe, Q6-balanced, Q4-aggressive) with annotations for model families + recommended minimum latency budgets. 3) SafePaths fallback policy: if runtime observes >5% token-level quality drift (measured by eval-set pass rate) or latency p95 increase beyond tenant budget, it automatically routes to the next safer path (higher quant precision, smaller batch, longer cold-cache warmup) and emits a rollback event. 4) econ-prober CLI: developer tool to run a dry-run against recorded traces or small live sample and produce a JSON report with recommended defaults and delta against current config. 5) docs + changelog and small UX additions in the Console for per-tenant recommendation previews.

Design notes and rationale: - We intentionally keep heuristics interpretable: rules are weighted simple metrics (seq distribution, qps burstiness, historical cost/unit) so SREs can reason and override. - Quant ladder is conservative by default: Q8-safe is the baseline for enterprise tier; Q4-aggressive is opt-in for low-cost experimental tenants. - SafePaths is a runtime guard; it's not a hard revert — it transitions traffic along a defined staircase of safer configurations and creates incidents when thresholds are hit. - econ-prober is shipped as an opt-in local tool to build confidence before applying tenant defaults to production.

Implementation highlights: - services/runtime/heuristics/tenant_defaults.go: new heuristics engine and evaluation harness. - services/runtime/batcher/tenant_batch_router.go: accepts suggested defaults and applies them to per-connection routing with a short-lived warmup window. - services/runtime/cache/prefix_ttl_manager.go: adds tenant TTL hints and cold-cache scorers. - compiler/quant/profiles.go: new quant ladder metadata and compatibility matrix per model family. - tooling/econ-prober/cli.go: CLI to run replay/dry-run and produce recommendation reports. - console/backend/api/tenant_recommendations.go: endpoint to surface recommendations. - docs/ops/tenant-cost-defaults.md: operational playbook and rollback steps.

Checklist (what I ran and why): - unit tests for heuristics scoring and quant compatibility (added +200 tests). - integration test with the batcher harness to verify SafePaths transitions under synthetic regression. - manual dry-runs with econ-prober on two tenant traces (search small-latency tenant, chat high-concurrency tenant). - load tests on canary cluster for 48h to ensure no steady-state throughput regressions. - docs and console UI smoke test.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main as feature-flag gated: --tenant-cost-heuristics. 2) Enable for internal tenants and alpha customers (canary pool) for 2 weeks. 3) Monitor unit-econ deltas, latency p95 and eval pass rates; use SafePaths to auto-mitigate if regressions detected. 4) Gradual ramp to more tenants after sign-off.

Metrics and observability: emitted metrics include heuristics.recommendation.apply_count, safe_paths.transition_count, econ_prober.reports_generated, tenant.quant_tier_changes, tenant.cache_ttl_hints. Traces instrumented for the batch route decision path. Dashboards added: "Tenant Cost Defaults" and alert: "SafePaths repeated transitions (>3 within 10m)".

Backout and safety: the feature is behind a kill-switch feature flag. SafePaths will gate regressions; we also added an emergency rollback CLI command and an automatic alert that surfaces the last applied recommendation blob.

Related work: references matching Linear tasks ENG-4332 (tenant defaults RFC), ENG-4401 (SafePaths policy spec), and SUP-1123 (support ticket motivating default recommendations).

Notes: prioritized interpretability and operator control over black-box optimization in this first iteration. Next steps: add learning loop that uses safe telemetry to refine weights and extend econ-prober to run comparative cost simulation across cloud SKUs.
